 Apayao sees minimal El Niño damage as rains start
 Nov 6, 2026
 10:27 AM GMT+8
 ‘NO MAJOR EFFECT FROM EL NIÑO.’ Apayao Governor Elias Bulut Jr. says Thursday (Nov. 5, 2026) that the province is not seeing a major effect from El Niño. He said rains have begun in Apayao, with the last quarter of the year to February being the rainy season. (PNA photo by Liza T. Agoot)
 LUNA, Apayao – The provincial government of Apayao said it is not seeing major agricultural losses from El Niño, with the province having a different rainy season.
 "Nag-start na ang rainy season. So, hopefully, that can contribute sa pagbawas ng effect ng El Niño. May damage talaga sa atin kasi nagiging dry ang lupa pero nag-start na, two weeks nang umuulan every afternoon (The rainy season has begun, which we hope will contribute to reducing the effects of El Niño. There will be damage because the soil dries up, but it has been raining for two weeks already)," Governor Elias Bulut Jr. said on Thursday.
 He added that rainwater will ensure springs are rejuvenated, and rivers increase their water level.
 Historically, Apayao's rainy season runs from October to February, sometimes extending to March.
 The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) has announced that the country will experience a strong El Niño in the last quarter of the year, progressing to a very strong El Niño in the first quarter of next year.
 Bulut also said most of their farmers who grow rice and corn have harvested their produce.
 "We are almost done," he said.
 He added that irrigated areas are just waiting for the status of the rainy season and might still plant for the second cropping when rainwater is ample for the rice plantation's irrigation.
 Meanwhile, Luna town Mayor Januario Garde said they are currently improving the town's potable and irrigation water system, which will take about three years to complete.
 "Rice and corn production are the primary source of livelihood of our people," he said. (PNA Liza T. Agoot)
